function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a given command using the os.system() function specifically for Windows operating systems. For multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For complex tasks, create and run a .bat file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The Windows command line instruction(s) to be executed. Use '&&' between commands for multiple instructions. For complex sequences, encapsulate the logic within a .bat file and provide the execution command here.

message.reasoning: The user says: "start Docker on window using docker start." They want to start Docker on Windows using docker start. But docker start is used to start containers, not the Docker service itself. To start Docker Desktop or Docker Engine, you might use services or Docker Desktop UI. On Windows, you can start Docker Desktop via the Start menu or run "Docker Desktop" executable. Or you can start the Docker service via PowerShell: Start-Service docker. Or use "net start com.docker.service". The user likely wants to start Docker engine. So we need to provide a command to start Docker service. We can use "cmd_controller_execute" to run "net start com.docker.service" or "Start-Service docker" in PowerShell. But the tool expects a Windows command line instruction. So we can do "net start com.docker.service". Let's do that.
